competitors.name: Food Lion
competitors.action: Grocery Dive reported Food Lion will open six additional stores across North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia before year-end, bringing 2026 openings to 10 after adding only one net new store in each of fiscal 2024 and 2025. The new stores will include ready-to-eat, ready-to-cook and ready-to-heat meals, Local Goodness regional items, pickup and delivery, and will be supported by Ahold Delhaize's planned Burlington, N.C., distribution center intended to expand fresh and frozen distribution.

competitors.name: Natural Grocers
competitors.action: Grocery Dive reported Natural Grocers' board approved reincorporating from Delaware to Texas, citing its roughly two dozen Texas stores and plans to keep expanding its footprint, workforce and customer base in the state. The specialty grocer is also targeting 4% to 5% annual new-store growth for the foreseeable future.

competitors.name: Harris Teeter
competitors.action: Grocery Dive reported Kroger-owned Harris Teeter plans to spend about $253 million over three years to upgrade Charlotte-area stores and develop three new locations in the Carolinas. Store changes may include layout and fixture upgrades, improved pickup and delivery, updated signage, and broader fresh, prepared-food and bakery assortments.

trends.topic: Regional grocers adding fresh, prepared and frozen capacity
trends.magnitude: Food Lion is opening 10 stores in 2026 and tying growth to fresh/frozen distribution; Harris Teeter is investing $253M in upgrades and three new stores.
trends.context: Regional banners are putting capital behind store experience, prepared meal options and cold-chain capacity. Premium frozen pizza needs to fit into both freezer productivity and retailer meal-solution strategies.

trends.magnitude: Natural Grocers is positioning Texas as a long-term growth market and targeting 4% to 5% annual new-store growth.
trends.context: Specialty grocery remains an expansion lane for natural and better-for-you products, but retailer growth is concentrated in markets where banners already have operational density.
